INTERVENTION: Implement "Cycling-Induced Calcification" by adjusting the DC rectifier output to cycle the pipe-to-soil potential between -1.15 V and -0.85 V vs. CSE, utilizing the 14-day cycling period to accelerate the kinetics of calcium carbonate deposition at coating defects to seal current drains and stabilize the static -0.85 V protection level.

PARAMETER: Pipeline Diameter — 36 inches — ASSUMPTION 
PARAMETER: Coating Type — Coal-tar enamel — ASSUMPTION 
PARAMETER: Target Static Potential — -0.85 V vs. CSE — ASSUMPTION (Standard NACE criterion for CP)
PARAMETER: Cycling Range — -1.15 V to -0.85 V vs. CSE — ASSUMPTION (Standard protocol for accelerating calcareous scaling)
PARAMETER: Cycling Period — 14 days — ASSUMPTION (Kinetic threshold for detectable mineral crust formation)
PARAMETER: Rectifier Power Budget — Fixed — EVIDENCE-BACKED [user variables]
PARAMETER: Excavation — Prohibited — EVIDENCE-BACKED [user variables]

MECHANISM AND EXPECTED EFFECT:
By temporarily driving the pipe-to-soil potential more negative than the static protection level (-1.15 V), the cathodic reaction rate is increased, driving the local pH to supersaturation levels required for calcium carbonate precipitation. This mineral crust forms preferentially on the steel surface and within coating defects ("holidays"), which act as high-current-density sites. As the defects are physically sealed by the calcareous scale, the total current demand of the pipeline decreases. This reduction in current demand allows the system to maintain the target -0.85 V static potential at the far ends of the 36-inch section without violating the fixed rectifier power budget. This intervention does not require excavation, as it relies entirely on the existing electrical infrastructure and the natural electrochemical process of calcareous scaling. The 1970s coal-tar enamel is not directly affected by the electrical potential, but the sealed defects prevent moisture ingress and localized corrosion.

FALSIFICATION TEST:
1. Test Temperature: 25 C (Assumed ambient soil temperature)
2. Duration: 28 days (Two 14-day cycling cycles to observe scaling progression)
3. Sample Size: n=3 representative far-end sections (Validation sample size to establish population-level threshold)
4. Pass/Fail Criteria: Pass if static pipe-to-soil potential stabilizes at -0.85 V vs. CSE at the far ends of all 3 sections after 28 days without exceeding the fixed power budget. Fail if potential remains below -0.85 V in any section or if hydrogen blistering is observed on the steel surface during post-test visual inspection.
